validation.notes: Regression script links the real resource-loader.ts, settings-manager.ts and project-trust.ts through .prale-eval/subject.mjs (only in-memory settings storage, trust-store writes, the project_trust event emitter and the package manager are faked) and drives the full untrusted-bootstrap -> resolver -> project-settings-reload chain. Verified: (1) resource-loader calls the trust resolver exactly once after the untrusted bootstrap, forwards the bootstrap LoadExtensionsResult, and the post-trust scan uses the granted state; (2) settings-manager actually clears/loads project settings on trust transitions, so approval loads project-model/project extensions and denial keeps them out; (3) project-trust persists an extension decision only for remember: true (approval and denial), never for remember: false or a missing remember, and the session-only prompt approval records no trust-store write while still granting access; (4) global configuration is unchanged in every scenario. Script 'node --experimental-vm-modules .prale-eval/regression.mjs' exits 0 on the repair. Fault isolation was checked by restoring each file individually to its faulty baseline: resource-loader (forced projectTrusted=false) -> 'resolver ... exactly once' fails with 0 !== 1; settings-manager (inverted early return) -> bootstrap extension scan runs trusted with project-model; project-trust (remember !== undefined) -> remember=false writes a trust-store entry. Each failure is a node:assert/strict AssertionError, not a crash, import error or timeout. Test state is promise-ordered only; no timers, randomness, network or credentials are used. Local test input is the .prale-eval/tmp-fixture sandbox root (with a link to the real packages directory) and is removed in a finally block. Limitation: packages are not installed in this workspace, so no TypeScript type-check or vitest suite could be run; module syntax/type stripping is exercised by the Node 24 run itself.
